sites.d: Once home to one of Singapore's oldest self-help organisations, the Former Keng Teck Whay Building is situated next to Thian Hock Keng.

sites.n: Former Singapore Conference Hall and Trade Union House (now Singapore Conference Hall)
sites.d: The Former Singapore Conference Hall and Trade Union House was constructed to house the headquarters of the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) as the fulfilment of an election promise.
Saint George's Church is situated in the quiet environs off Minden Road, a short distance from the bustling shopping district of Orchard Road.
Saint Joseph's Church on Victoria Street was the headquarters of the Portuguese Mission in Singapore.
Dwarfed by modern skyscrapers in the heart of the Central Business District is one of Singapore's oldest Chinese temples, Yueh Hai Ching Temple.
Located on Telok Ayer Street, a short walk from Thian Hock Keng, the Former Keng Teck Whay Building, and the Former Nagore Dargah, Al-Abrar Mosque is one of Singapore's oldest mosques.
The College of Medicine Building is located at the rear of the Singapore General Hospital's compound, next to Tan Teck Guan Building.
Like the nearby Sri Mariamman Temple, Jamae Mosque has been a familiar landmark on South Bridge Road since the mid-nineteenth century.
Located not far from the Istana and the Former Cathay Building, MacDonald House has a relatively plain and unadorned facade that does not appear to be exceptionally striking.

sites.n: Former Siong Lim Temple (now Lian Shan Shuang Lin Monastery)
sites.d: The traditional architecture of Lian Shan Shuang Lin Monastery - or 'Twin Grove Monastery on Lotus Hill' - stands out amidst the modern high-rise apartment blocks in the Toa Payoh neighbourhood.
The Former Nagore Dargah is situated on the historic Telok Ayer Street, a short distance from Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church, Al-Abrar Mosque and Thian Hock Keng.
Prinsep Street Presbyterian Church is one of Singapore's oldest Presbyterian churches.
Originally known as the Chinese Methodist Church, Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church was the first church established to cater exclusively to the spiritual needs of the Chinese Methodist community.
Fort Siloso was one of the many coastal fortifications built around the 19th century by the British and remains the most intact fortification in Singapore.
The Padang is one of the oldest open spaces in Singapore for public recreation and a commemorative space for people to gather, witness and participate in key milestones of Singapore�s history.

Built between the 1930s-1950s, these blocks are representative buildings of the former KKH and showcase the hospital�s instrumental role in advancing midwifery, maternal, and gynaecological care in Singapore.
The site at 38 Oxley Road bore witness to pivotal events in the 1950s that marked Singapore�s transition from a colony to an independent nation.
Formerly the royal mosque of the Sultan of Johor, Sultan Mosque represents the solidarity and unity of Muslims in Singapore.

sites.n: Former Empress Place Building (now Asian Civilisations Museum)
sites.d: Situated at the mouth of the Singapore River, the Former Empress Place Building was an important government building in Singapore up to the 1980s.
The Tower Wing of the present-day Goodwood Park Hotel was home to the German Teutonia Club, one of the earliest European national clubs in Singapore.
Standing beside the College of Medicine Building is a smaller, two-storey building known as Tan Teck Guan Building.

sites.n: Changi Prison Gate Wall and Turrets
sites.d: Changi Prison was designed to be a maximum security prison to house up to 600 criminals sentenced to long-term imprisonment in British Singapore.

sites.n: Former Saint Joseph's Institution (now Singapore Art Museum)
sites.d: Saint Joseph's Institution is the oldest Catholic boys' school in Singapore and was founded by the Christian Brothers (formally known as the Institute of the Brothers of the Christian Schools)

sites.n: Former Attorney-Generals Chambers (now Parliament House Block C)
sites.d: Tucked away in a corner near the Padang is a beautiful structure that once housed the Attorney-General's Chambers.

sites.n: Former Nanyang University Library and Administration Building, Memorial and Arch
sites.d: Nanyang University, affectionately known as Nantah, was the first Chinese-language university in Southeast Asia and the second university in Singapore.

sites.n: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
sites.d: The Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary is one of the earliest Catholic churches built in the suburbs of Singapore.

sites.n: Former Convent of the Holy Infant Jesus Chapel and Caldwell House (now CHIJMES)
sites.d: Owing to its central location, the Convent of the Holy Infant Jesus was also affectionately referred to as the Town Convent in the past.
Abdul Gafoor Mosque's charming architecture stands out amidst the surrounding shophouses in the historic Little India district.

sites.n: Church of Saints Peter and Paul
sites.d: The Church of Saints Peter and Paul is one of the oldest Catholic churches in Singapore that catered to a predominantly Chinese congregation.
The Chinese High School Clock Tower Building is the icon of the oldest Chinese-medium high school in Singapore and has been a visual landmark of Bukit Timah Road since its completion.
Within the historic district of Kampong Gelam lies Istana Kampong Gelam ('Gelam Village Palace').
Chesed-El Synagogue on Oxley Rise is one of two synagogues in Singapore, the other being Maghain Aboth Synagogue on Waterloo Street.
Located in the heart of the Civic District, the Former City Hall served as an important government office in Singapore.
Hajjah Fatimah Mosque is one of the oldest mosques in Singapore, a rare example of one named after a woman.
Amidst the colonial buildings and skyscrapers of the Civic District rises the copper-green dome of the Former Supreme Court.
Formerly known as Sri Narasimha Perumal Temple, Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple is the first Hindu temple in Singapore dedicated to Sri Perumal, the Hindu deity more commonly known as Vishnu.
The Cathedral of the Good Shepherd is Singapore's oldest Catholic place of worship and the seat of the local Roman Catholic archbishop.
Alkaff Upper Serangoon Mosque was constructed by the mercantile and landowning Alkaff family to serve the spiritual needs of the local Muslim community at large.
On a hill overlooking Jurong estate, Jurong Town Hall once served as the headquarters of Jurong Town Corporation (JTC, presently JTC Corporation).
Shielded from the bustling Orchard Road by a sprawling green lung, the Istana ('Palace' in Malay) is the official residence of the President of the Republic of Singapore.

sites.n: Former Telok Ayer Market (now known as Lau Pa Sat)
sites.d: Affectionately known as Lau Pa Sat ('Old Market') by generations of Singaporeans, the Former Telok Ayer Market was one of Singapore's oldest markets.

sites.n: Former Ministry of Labour Building (now Family Justice Courts)
sites.d: The Former Ministry of Labour Building is located not far away from the Former Thong Chai Medical Institution and Tan Si Chong Su.
Together with Jamae Mosque, Sri Mariamman Temple - Singapore's oldest Hindu temple - is an enduring icon on South Bridge Road which is a part of Chinatown.
Thian Hock Keng ('Palace of Heavenly Happiness') is one of Singapore's oldest Hokkien temples.
Sri Thendayuthapani Temple, commonly referred to as the Chettiars' Temple, is one of Singapore's oldest Hindu temples dedicated to Murugan, the Hindu deity who is also known as Sri Thendayuthapani.
Saint Andrew's Cathedral is Singapore's oldest surviving Anglican place of worship and is the seat of the Anglican bishop of Singapore.
The history of Tan Si Chong Su ('Ancestral Hall of the Tan Clan') is inextricably linked to the influx of Chinese immigrants into Singapore during the late nineteenth century.
The former Fullerton Building is a prominent landmark situated at the mouth of the Singapore River.
In the heart of Singapore's historic Civic District stand the magnificent Victoria Theatre and Victoria Concert Hall with the iconic clock tower.
Not far from Former Nagore Dargah on Telok Ayer Street is Ying Fo Fui Kun, Singapore's oldest Hakka clan association.

sites.n: Armenian Apostolic Church of Saint Gregory the Illuminator
sites.d: The Armenian Apostolic Church of Saint Gregory the Illuminator - commonly called the Armenian Church - is Singapore's oldest Christian church
The Art Deco facade wall fronting the modern glass architecture of The Cathay is the remnant of what used to be Malaya's tallest building.

Home to the first free traditional Chinese medical clinic for the poor in Singapore, the Former Thong Chai Medical Institution testifies to the Chinese pioneers' spirit of mutual assistance and their generosity towards the poor and needy.
Tou Mu Kung Temple is the oldest temple in Singapore dedicated to the Taoist deity Jiu Huang Ye ('Nine Emperors' or 'Ninth Emperor').
Standing atop a little hill, the Church of Saint Teresa was originally constructed for the spiritual needs of the Hokkien-speaking Catholics living in the town area.
The Former Saint James Power Station was the first coal-fired power station on the island.
The Former Tanjong Pagar Railway Station was previously the southernmost terminal station of the Federated Malay States Railways.
Not far from the Esplanade Park Memorials stands the Civilian War Memorial, the first memorial in Singapore dedicated to the civilian victims of the Japanese Occupation (1942-1945).

sites.n: Chung Cheng High School (Main) Administration Building and Entrance Arch
sites.d: As one of Singapore's oldest Chinese high schools, Chung Cheng High School was among the firsts to make higher education accessible to Chinese youth.
Nicknamed the 'Police Skyscraper' in the past, the Former Hill Street Police Station is prominently located at the junction of Hill Street and River Valley Road.
With its wide facade and large dome, the National Museum of Singapore has been a prominent landmark on Stamford Road for over a century.

sites.n: Church of Our Lady of Lourdes
sites.d: Known simply as the Indian Church or Tamil Church in the past, the Church of Our Lady of Lourdes is one of Singapore's oldest Catholic churches.

sites.n: Former House of Tan Yeok Nee
sites.d: Standing out prominently from its modern surroundings, the Chinese-style Former House of Tan Yeok Nee is the sole survivor of the 'Four Grand Mansions' built in the late nineteenth-century.
Hong San See ('Temple on Phoenix Hill'), perched on the side of Institution Hill off Mohamed Sultan Road, was established by Hokkien immigrants from Nan'an (or Lam Ann) County in Fujian Province.

sites.n: Former Tao Nan School (now The Peranakan Museum)
sites.d: A stone's throw from the Armenian Church is a century-old building that used to house Tao Nan School, the first modern Chinese school in Singapore.

sites.n: Former Ford Factory (now Memories at Old Ford Factory)
sites.d: Built atop a little hill, the Former Ford Factory has been a visual landmark in Bukit Timah since its completion in 1941.

sites.n: Former Raffles College (now NUS Campus at Bukit Timah)
sites.d: Located next to the Singapore Botanic Gardens, the Former Raffles College is well hidden from the public eye.
Amidst the modern blocks in the sprawling compound of Singapore General Hospital stands a Neoclassical building with its distinctive clock tower.

The stately Former Command House is located near Bukit Timah Road, a major road constructed during the mid-nineteenth century and one of the last defences against the invading Japanese troops in 1942.
Prior to the first land reclamation in 1843, the original shoreline of Singapore ran across the present Padang.

sites.n: Former Parliament House and Annex Building (now The Arts House)
sites.d: The Former Parliament House is likely to be the oldest surviving building in Singapore.
Raffles Hotel is one of the most well-known luxury hotels in Singapore and the oldest surviving establishment of its kind on the island.

sites.n: Former Sun Yat Sen Villa (now Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall)
sites.d: Sun Yat-sen Nanyang Memorial Hall is one of the few surviving examples of villas that were once common sights in British Singapore.

sites.n: Singapore River Bridges: Cavenagh Bridge, Anderson Bridge and Elgin Bridge
sites.d: Cavenagh, Anderson and Elgin Bridges are the three most historic and architecturally impressive bridges that span the Singapore River. Collectively, they illustrate Singapore's growth as a trading port and flourishing city. Located at the h
Surrounded by several ancillary buildings and facilities on a sprawling estate, the Former Admiralty House used to accommodate key military commanders based in Singapore.
Located in the former Jewish neighbourhood, Maghain Aboth Synagogue is the oldest surviving synagogue not only in Singapore, but also in Southeast Asia.
The Central Fire Station is the oldest surviving fire station in Singapore and is a living monument to the local firefighting force.
Fort Canning Command Centre was the site where Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival and his commanders decided to surrender Singapore to the Japanese on 15 February 1942.
Keppel Harbour has been a thriving maritime gateway for trade since the late 19th century. During the Second World War, Operation Jaywick successfully destroyed seven Japanese ships here.
During the Second World War, the last Allied military troop in Malaya withdrew to Singapore through the Causeway on 31 January 1942, after losing Malaya to the Japanese.
Yeung Ching School began in 1905 as a private school for Cantonese children. Apart from conducting classes in the day, it offered night classes to children who were poor or overaged.
Raffles Place was designated as Singapore's business centre in the 1822 Town Plan. Singapore's earliest banks, merchant houses and department stores were situated here.
The Mental Hospital was completed in 1928 at Yio Chu Kang Road. It was renamed "Woodbridge Hospital" after a nearby wooden bridge, and then "The Institute of Mental Health" after moving here in 1993.
From a small gate here, the compassionate sisters of the Convent of the Holy Infant Jesus took in many abandoned infants and children. A replica, named "Gate of Hope", was installed here in 1996.
UEL was founded in 1912. It led major construction projects that contributed to Singapore's urbanisation and economic growth, and built many iconic structures including the Former Supreme Court.

sites.n: Execution of Captured Rimau Commandos Historic Marker
sites.d: Operation Rimau ("tiger" in Malay) was the second Allied commando attack on Japanese ships in Keppel Harbour. It failed, and ten commandos were beheaded by the Japanese near Dover and Clementi Roads.

From 1881, Sikh men began arriving in Singapore as part of the Straits Settlement Police�s Sikh Contingent. Along with the Upper Barracks at the top of this hill, this 5-Storey building was completed in 1934 to house the men.
Seletar Airfield was the British Royal Air Force's main base in the Far East, equipped to protect the Sembawang naval base. Indian Prisoners-of-War were interned here during the Japanese Occupation.
This 3-Storey building, along with the Lower Barracks, on Pearl�s Hill were built in 1934 specifically as residence for the Sikh Contingent of the Straits Settlement Police.
This was the headquarters of Singapore Customs from 1932 to 1989. The building also housed the Film Censor's Office and the Maxwell Road Post Office.
Located in the central area of Singapore, bordering Lornie Road and parts of the Pan-Island Expressway, Bukit Brown Cemetery (BBC) was the first Chinese municipal cemetery in colonial Singapore.

Vutthisara, a monk from Thailand, founded the temple in 1927. This site is selected as both Indians and Chinese in an area predominantly settled it. It houses a Buddha statue of 15m talls and weighing 300 tonnes.
The local INA, influenced by Subhas Chandra Bose, was formed in 1942 with Japanese support, with the aim of liberating India from British.

This was the site of sporting activities in the early days and became popular with families. In 1953, as part of the Coronation Celebrations, the seafront promenade was refurbished and renamed Queen Elizabeth Walk.

Formerly housing the British Malaya Broadcasting Corporations before WWII, it was turned into a Japanese propaganda office during the Japanese Occupation. It was later also used by Lord Louis Mountbatten as the headquarters for the Japanese
On 8 February 1942, Japanese forces first landed in Singapore on this beach.
It was here on 9 February 1942 that the Japanese forces suffered a major loss, fighting against the valiant 27th Australian Brigade and the Dalforce.
The Battle for Pasir Panjang, where the harbour and British military depots were the coveted gains, marked one of the last battles for Singapore. It lasted from 12 to 14 February 1942.
This site marks one of many temporary registration centres set up by the Kempeitai(Japanese Military Police) to screen anti-Japanese Chinese.

Trinity Theological College was born out of the camaraderie and spirit of Christianity experienced by the heads of the Anglican, Methodist and Presbyterian Churches when they were interned at Changi Prison during the Japanese Occupation. Fo
Designed by colonial engineer, John Bennett, the theatre portion of the Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall was built as a Town Hall in 1862 which housed the Municipal Offices.

Farrer Park was the site of the first race course in Singapore, and continued to be a venue for numerous sporting events. It was a site for political gatherings and demonstrations in the 1940s and 1950s.
This temple was built in 1870 and is one of the oldest Hindu temples in Singapore.
Pulau Sejahat was designated as a British defence outpost. The military encampment on the island included gun emplacements, water tanks and observation towers.

sites.n: Kwan Im Thong Hood Cho Temple
sites.d: This temple was built in 1884, showcasing a fine example of Chinese temple architecture and traditional craftsmanship. The temple played an important role in providing refuge for the sick, the wounded and the homeless during the Japanese Oc
This is Singapore's second reservoir, constructed after water demand outgrew the capacity of MacRitchie Reservoir. It was known as Kalang River Reservoir when it opened in 1912.
Singapore's first reservoir was officially opened in 1878 as the Impounding Reservoir, to supply freshwater for the growing population. It has also been a popular place for recreation over the years.
On 1 October 1935, UOB opened for business at the Bonham Building in Raffles Place. Over the years, it grew to become one of Singapore's leading banks.
This is Singapore's first purpose-built civil airport. Completed in 1937, the modern-style terminal building symbolised the rapid civil aviation progress then. The airport ceased operations in 1955.
Clifford Pier was the landing point for sea passengers and immigrants who came to seek a new life in Singapore. It is also known as "Red Lantern Pier" for the red lamps that hung here.
Singapore Badminton Hall was built to host international badminton tournaments. In 1962, it was a vote-counting station for the Referendum on Singapore's merger with Malaya, Sabah and Sarawak.
Pearl's Hill School began in 1876 at Cross Street as the Singapore Chinese Branch School. It was among the first English elementary schools established by the colonial government.
Jalan Besar Stadium was Singapore's main football arena until the National Stadium opened. It also hosted various national events, such as Singapore Youth Festival and National Day Parade.
Raffles Girls' School began in 1844 as a girls' department in Singapore Institution (today Raffles Institution), and became independent in 1879. It was located here from 1928 to 1979.
Singapore Chinese Girls' School began in 1899 at Hill Street. It was founded by Straits Chinese pioneers to provide quality education for girls. The school was located here from 1925 to 1994.

This is one of the surviving gun emplacements in Singapore today. The battery has two 6" 16-ton guns facing south, which aided the Malay Regiment in the Battle for Pasir Panjang by firing high explosive shells at the advancing Japanese troo

Opened in 1940, the Alexandra Hospital (former British Military Hospital) served as the principal hospital for Britain's Far East Command during World War II. The hospital was the most-advanced and best-equipped medical institution in Singa

Originally known as Deng Xiansheng and his school name Deng Xixian, Deng Xiaoping was born on 22 August 1904 in Guang'an County, Sichuan Province. In 1920, Deng left forÂ studies in France. His six-year stay in France proved to be a turning

Kandang Kerbau Hospital, the birthplace of over 1.2 million Singaporeans, was the largest maternity hospital in the world from the early 1950s to the early 1970s. It was named after the district where it was located. The district around the
The first school in Singapore, it was founded by Sir Stamford Raffles on 5 June 1823. It was originallly known as "The Institution".

Established in 1918 by Chinese Immigrants from the Jin Jiang County of southern Fujian Province, it was the headquarters of the Overseas Chinese Mobilisation Council, formed in 1941 to help Singapore's defence against the Japanese.
This temple was built by Ceylon Tamils. It began in an attap shed under a champak ("senpaga" in Tamil) tree in 1875, located near the discovery site of a statue of Vinayagar (the deity Ganesha).
Queenstown was built in 1960s to meet housing shortage in Singapore after the Second World War. It is Singapore's first satellite town â€“ an estate with amenities to meet residents' needs.
Batu Berlayar ("Sailing Rock"), together with a rock on the opposite shore of Tanjong Rimau, formed a gateway to the west of Keppel Harbour. It was blown up in 1848 to widen the harbour's entrance.
Geylang Serai is a social centre for the Malay community in Singapore. It was originally filled with lemongrass ("serai" in Malay) plantations between the 1890s to early 1900s.
Singapore's last pondok (communal lodging house) was located here from 1932 to 2000. It served the welfare of Baweanese immigrants from the Gelam province of Indonesia's Bawean Island.

sites.n: The Founding of Boys' Brigade in Singapore
sites.d: Singapore's first company of the Boys' Brigade was formed here on 12 January 1930. From a small company of 12, the Boys' Brigade in Singapore has since grown to a strength of more than 100 companies.
This building housed Fuk Tak Chi ("Fu De Ci" in Mandarin), one of the Singapore's oldest Chinese temples, from the 1820s to 1994. It was later converted into a museum.

OCBC Bank was formed in 1932 through the merger of three Hokkien banks. It was originally located at China Building which featured a prominent Chinese-style roof and classical elements on its faÃ§ade.
Singapore's third reservoir was constructed in 1920 to meet the increased demand for freshwater in Singapore. The iconic lookout tower was added to the reservoir in the 1960s.
Established in 1820, Omar Kampong Malacca Mosque is Singapore's oldest mosque. In the 1850s, the original timber structure made way for the current building to accommodate the mosque's growing needs.

In the early days of the SAF and Singapore's independence, the Singapore Infantry Regiment and the PDF shouldered the duties of national defence. The Beach Road Army Camp played a significant role in the transformation.
Officially opened on 8 August 1963, this theatre was built to commemorate the attainment of Singapore's self-government in 1959. It was demolished in 1986 due to structural reasons.
United Chinese Library was founded by Dr Sun Yat Sen on 8 August 1910 at North Boat Quay, to spread revolutionary ideas and garner support for Dr Sun's revolution in China.
Completed in the late 1930s, Johore Battery was part of Singapore's coastal defence system. It comprised three 15-inch guns known as "monster guns".
Merdeka Bridge, declared open on 17 August 1956, was constructed to ease traffic congestion. Its name reflects Singapore's aspirations for independence ("merdeka" in Malay) then.
This was formerly the home of Chen Wen Hsi, one of Singapore's pioneer artists. Chen's works mixed Western and Chinese traditions, and continued to influence local artists after his demise in 1991.
Methodist Girls' School began in 1887 as Tamil Girls' School in a shophouse at Short Street with nine Indian girls.
St. Margaret's School began as a girls' home at North Bridge Road in 1842, to rescue girls who were homeless or being sold to slavery.
Built in 1862, Kallang Gasworks was Singapore's first supplier of piped gas. It played an important role in ensuring efficient gas production for Singapore.

Founded in 1895, it is one of the oldest millionaires club in Singapore. The club was the centre of the Chinese Salvation Movement in Southeast Asia from 1937-1942. Originally located at Duxton Hill, it moved to Club Street before settling
Changi Beach was a massacre site of Sook Ching. The Hojo Kempei (Japanese auxiliary military police) machine-gunned many male civilians on this shore on 20 February 1942.
Adam park estate was the site of intense fighting between British forces and the invading Japanese army in February 1942, in the last days before the British surrendered Singapore.

The Anglo-Chinese School (ACS) was founded by Rev. William Fitzjames Oldham in 1886 at a shophouse in Amoy Street. Starting with 13 students, the school aimed to provide an education for the many boys Bishop Fitzjames saw wandering aimlessl

Balestier Road, from which Balestier Plain takes its name, was named after Joseph Balestier, a keen botanist and agriculturist who arrived in Singapore in 1834. He was appointed as the first U.S Consul in Singapore in 1836 by then President
Outram Road Prison was the main jail in Singapore until Changi Prison opened in 1937. Thereafter, it became a remand prison, housing opium addicts, juvenile delinquents, and political detainees.
This hospital was founded in 1844 by Tan Tock Seng, a philanthropic Hokkien Chinese pioneer, for the poor and destitute. Here, several firsts in Singapore's medical history were achieved.
The Changi Murals was a symbol of hope and faith for prisoners during the Japanese Occupation. It depicted scenes from the Bible, and were painted by Stanley Warren, a Prisoner-of-War.

Founded in 1826, this club became the Royal Singapore Yacht Club in 1922 under the patronage of the Prince of Wales, and was renamed the Republic of Singapore Yacht Club in 1967 with the first president of Singapore, Yusof bin Ishak as it p

Built between 1870-75, the Middle Road Church was first known as the Christian Institute. When it was officially inaugurated as the Malay Church in 1894, it became the first Straits Chinese Methodist Church in Singapore.

Syonan Jinja was built in 1942 in memory of the Japanese soldiers who died fighting in the invasion of Singapore. Ceremonies for significant events were held here until it was destroyed after the war.

One of the fiercest military encounters during WWII took place here as the Bukit Timah area held strategic and tactical importance to the Japanese and the British. This site marks Percival's final defence of southern Singapore against the J

Two memorials, one for the Japanese soldiers and the other for Allied Soldiers sat on top on this hill-top. The former was Syonan Chureito, built by 500 Allied Prisoners of War while the latter was a wooden cross that stood behind.
Also known as the Wadda Gurdwara, this Sikh temple was the first set up in a bungalow at Queen Street in 1912. The temple is now relocated at Towner Road.

The original building, the YMCA, was used by the East Branch of the Kempeitai (Japanese Military Police) during the Japanese Occupation. Local anti-Japanese suspects were imprisoned and tortured for information here. The building was pulled
Sime Road Camp was the Combined Headquarters of the British Army and Air Force during the Second World War, until the headquarters relocated to Fort Canning Command Centre.

sites.n: Havelock Road Camp / River Valley Road Camp
sites.d: The area bounded by River Valley Road and Havelock Road was occupied by Prisoner-of-War (POW) camps during the Japanese Occupation. Five thousand POWs lived in dilapidated attap huts here.

This is one of the oldest parks in Singapore. Built in the 1930s, it was a favourite place for families and couples, with facilities such as swimming bays which extended into the sea and food outlets.

In the early 1900s, Singapore grew rapidly and the crime rate rose with the city's expansion. Harold Fariburn - the Inspector - General of Police from 1925 to 1935 - realised that the Police needed a programme of modernisation and expansion

Chui Eng Free School was established here in 1854 by the Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan. It was the second-oldest private Chinese school and also one of the first free educational institutions in Singapore.
Surrendered British Gunners awaiting Japanese internment buried some 300 bullet-ridden corpses washed ashore on Pulau Blakang Mati, now known as Sentosa.

In 1885, Gan Eng Seng founded a free school for poor boys in Singapore. Initially named the Anglo-Chinese Free School, it was among the earliest schools to offer a bilingual education. The school moved to its first new building about 50 met
This pillbox was located inland to provide fire cover and defence for key installations in Bukit Timah during the Second World War.

This pillbox lay within the area guarded by the 1st Battalion of the Malay Regiment during the Second World War, to protect key installations in the Southern area, such as Alexandra Military Hospital.
Established in 1954, Singapore Polytechnic is the first technical institution in Singapore to train skilled labour. The Prince Edward Campus began operations on 3 November 1958 with 2,800 students.
This is an arbitrary defence line from Kranji River to Jurong River, placed to check Japanese advance towards the city from the west.
Punggol Beach was a massacre site of Sook Ching. Several men were killed by the Hojo Kempei (Japanese auxiliary military police) on this beach on 28 February 1942.

sites.n: Singapore Armed Forces Warrant Officers' and Specialists' Club
sites.d: The British Government built the clubhouse in 1951 for British non-commissioned officers. It was handed over to Singapore Government when the British pulled out in 1969.The SAF WOSE club was formed in 1974 and was formerly known as the SAF
This temple was built in 1924 on Silat Road (today Jalan Bukit Merah). It was also known as the Police Gurdwara (a Sikh place of worship) as its congregation was mostly made up of Sikh policemen.

sites.n: The First Public Dental School and Public Clinic
sites.d: Dental Education and modern dentistry in Singapore began here in 1929. The original Clinic and Dental School of the King Edward VII college of Medicine had its beginnings on this site in the Norris Block of the General Hospital. In 1938, th

Joseph Conrad, the renowned English master writer, was of Polish origin and travelled to Singapore and south east asia during his seafaring days. He made Singapore and Southeast asia better known to the world through his writings.
Force 136 was a British secret service team that operated in Malaya during the Second World War. One of the agents was Lim Bo Seng, who led Gustavus V Operation in 1943. His grave is in the vicinity.
